extrapolated_research.note: linear extrapolation from the measured acceptance run, no guaranteed upper bound; the release gate's permutations grow with the contexts as well (see lr5/lr5_budget.json)

operating_window.basis: Astra, review LANTERN_LR6_REVIEW_29af52f sections 1 and 9: at least 2.5 h including the release report and a possible resume
operating_window.rule: the 20 contexts and the evaluation rules are fixed; a runtime problem is never a reason to drop contexts after results were seen

claims_scope: a positive result concerns the documented dynamics, measurement map, Ridge readability and the concrete structural reference; it shows no biological or physical transfer. 20 contexts are a resource decision, not a demonstrated power: a negative result is reported as not reaching the prespecified evidence.

alarms.positive_spurious_success: any cell with observed G > 0 AND Holm-adjusted p <= 0.01 (the plan's alarm on unexpectedly positive G)
alarms.reported: both alarms with every cell's G, p and Holm p, under these two separate names; never merged into one flag
alarms.target_dependence: any cell with Holm-adjusted p <= 0.01 regardless of the sign of G (reset/zero impulse: a control decoder that depends recognisably on the test target; permuted targets: a control decoder better than label-free refits, even when worse than the zero prediction)

cells.names: '{control}|{task}|{tau}', in exactly this nested order (controls, tasks, times) = Holm family order
cells.rule: control x task x tau, decoder Ridge, coupling condition lantern

controls.permuted_targets: states and features as in the main condition; the TRAINING targets are permuted by the decoder stream (study, context, train, decoder, 0, extra 2, task index, time index) and the VALIDATION targets by (study, context, val, decoder, 0, extra 3, task index, time index) before fit and lambda selection; test targets stay real; full 7-time curves are reported
controls.reset: write, then reset to phi * 1 at once (encoding control 'reset'); full 7-time curves are reported
controls.zero_impulse: nothing is written (encoding control 'zero_impulse'); full 7-time curves are reported

release_rule.implemented_default: the release gate applies this rule (both alarms block)
release_rule.interpretation: both names denote the same directional test (per cell family its own null), with and without the additional condition G > 0; a missing alarm does not prove independence
release_rule.investigation: an investigation is no automatic override: finding, cause, consequences and, if needed, a new protocol version are documented
release_rule.proposal: either alarm sets scientifically_interpretable = false and blocks the scientific release until a documented investigation; a negative G does not make a target dependence harmless; technically_complete is unaffected by the alarms
release_rule.status: ENDORSED by Johann and Astra (REVIEW_LR5, 2026-10-09); becomes binding with the research freeze (LR6)

revision.v2: investigation results/lantern/lr6_acceptance_investigation/UNTERSUCHUNG.md: the test predictions of a label-permuted decoder CAN depend on the test targets because its features carry target information (shown in the diagnosed case: task A, early times), so the fixed-prediction null was the wrong comparison for these cells and fired there (only in permuted_targets|A|1.0); in addition lambda selection on REAL validation targets is a weak channel of target information. v2: validation targets are permuted too, and the four permuted-target cells use a refit null; reset and zero_impulse are unchanged
revision.v3: review LANTERN_LR6_REVIEW_29af52f R2: with constant features the observed fit and every refit give mathematically the SAME gain, but fit_ridge + scoring and the vectorised refits differed by round-off (4.16e-17); the exact comparison counted 0 of 9999 ties and reported p = 0.0001 (Holm 0.0012, target-dependence alarm) instead of p = 1. v3 adds the tie rule and the refit-path check (statistic.tie_rule, statistic.refit_path_check); cells, streams, B and the alarms are unchanged

control_alarms.source: plan v2.0 section 10 (empirical controls); review LANTERN_LR4_NACHREVIEW_25ba293 LR5-A1

statistic.multiplicity: Holm over ALL 12 cells at 0.01, always; never only over a selected subset (e.g. the positive cells)
statistic.p_value: p = (1 + b) / (1 + B), b = number of null statistics >= observed - tie_rule.absolute_tolerance (ties count toward the upper tail)
statistic.per_cell: observed mean over the contexts of G (projected test predictions of the fitted control decoder)
statistic.permuted_targets: refit null: per context B = 9999 gains of the COMPLETE procedure with NEW train and val permutations (refit, lambda selection, test on the real targets), stream (study, context, train, decoder, 0, extra 4, task index, time index), computed during the run and stored as the cell's null.npz; null statistic of draw b = mean over contexts of the b-th gains

refit_path_check.rule: per permuted-target alarm cell and context, the observed gain is computed twice: by the cell's fitted decoder (fit_ridge + scoring, the value that is recorded and enters the statistic) and by the SAME vectorised refit code as the null draws (training.refit_gains) with the cell's own train and val permutations; their absolute difference must be <= 1e-12, else the cell is refused (the numerical contract behind the tie rule does not hold). Both values and the difference are stored with the cell's null provenance

statistic.reset_and_zero_impulse: their features carry no target information: test targets permuted WITHIN each context, predictions fixed; B = 9999; one generator per cell (study, context 0, test, decoder, 0, extra 1, cell index), the contexts permuted from it in ascending order

tie_rule.applies_to: every control-alarm cell: the refit null of the permuted-target cells AND the fixed-prediction null of reset/zero_impulse
tie_rule.direction: conservative: a null statistic within the tolerance BELOW the observed one counts as a tie, i.e. toward the upper tail; this can only raise p, never lower it
tie_rule.reason: G is a mean of bounded losses (targets and projected predictions in [-1, 1], so -12 <= G <= 3). Mathematically equal statistics computed along different floating-point paths differ only by round-off; the refit-path check below bounds the fit-versus-refit difference per cell at 1e-12 and refuses the cell otherwise, so 1e-10 is 100 times that checked bound. It is absolute, not relative, because G can be 0. Measured on development data (dev contexts 0-3, the four refit cells): fit-versus-refit at most 7.5e-18, refit draws versus fit_ridge at most 8.7e-18. The spread of real null statistics is far larger (second development acceptance run: SD of the cell's null statistic 3.8e-5 to 2.5e-3; in none of the 12 cells was a null statistic within 1e-10 of the observed one, smallest distance 1.3e-9), so the band changes the expected count by about B x density x 1e-10 << 1. Fixed from the error bound, before any research run; not chosen from a p-value.

control_rules.structure_check: reset and zero impulse identical for u and -u (first 8 test episodes per context, lantern)

mlp.basis: proposed by Claude (first candidate, 29af52f); endorsed by Astra (review LANTERN_LR6_REVIEW_29af52f, section 1); binding only with the freeze approval
mlp.reason: plan 6/8: Ridge is primary and does not block on the MLP; the MLP was never implemented or validated (initialisation, regularisation and early stopping are unspecified in code), and plan 13 names it as the first item to drop under budget pressure. A later MLP needs its own protocol version.
mlp.scope_of_statements: every statement is limited to the examined Ridge readability; a negative result proves no general non-readability by other decoders

decoder.objective: (1/N) ||X_s W + 1 b^T - U||_F^2 + lambda ||W||_F^2  (X_s standardised features; intercept b unpenalised)
decoder.projection: main loss on predictions clipped to [-1, 1]; raw predictions are kept
decoder.selection: smallest validation MSE of the PROJECTED predictions; on an exactly equal value the larger lambda
decoder.standardisation: mean and population SD (ddof 0) of the TRAINING features only; an exactly constant column (all values identical) gets mean = its value and scale 1

inference.task_A: estimation: mean, SD, pointwise two-sided 95% t interval of A_lantern, A_uncoupled and their paired difference

allowed_statements.False|False: the pre-specified evidence was not reached; this is no general impossibility proof
allowed_statements.False|True: H-B2 alone without H-B1: no statement of distributed readability; report descriptively
allowed_statements.True|False: distributed readability shown; no demonstrated specific advantage over the structural reference
allowed_statements.True|True: distributed readability and an advantage over this strength surrogate under the protocol

task_B.test: one-sided t on context values minus margin; Holm over exactly these two at 0.05; Bonferroni intervals at t .9875, df = contexts - 1
